literal: Prosperity, inquiring the path, will go to the presence of him who has wavering-less energy.
translation: Prosperity will ask for the way and go on its own to the presence of one who possesses unwavering energy.
modern: தளர்ச்சி இல்லாத ஊக்கத்தை உடையவனிடம், செல்வமானது தானே வழியைக் கேட்டுக்கொண்டு போய்ச் சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the magnetic power of persistent, unwavering energy (ūkkam). Instead of a person having to struggle and search for wealth, the poet personifies prosperity (ākkam) as an active seeker. Prosperity itself will ask for directions ('atar viṉāy') to find the path that leads directly to the side ('uḻai') of the person who never wavers or gives up ('acaivilā'). The word 'acaivu' here refers to slackness, hesitation, or discouragement, making 'acaivilā' the quality of being steadfast and resolute.
